activity.title: Little Loaves
activity.goal: Strengthen little hands by squeezing, rolling and patting.
materials: Two slices of soft bread (gluten-free if needed)

steps.caption: Tear the bread into the bowl.
The grown-up adds one spoon of water.
Squeeze, roll, pat. A little loaf!
Hot, hot! Hands back. Then wash hands.

activity.safety: Ask about wheat allergy first. Bread only: never raw flour or play dough. A taste is fine: a small flat piece, eaten sitting down. If there is an accident, call your local emergency number.
activity.forAdult: In the story, Dina pulls her hands back and waits when Uncle says “Hot!” This activity keeps the bakery feeling with no heat at all, because the bread is already baked. Squeezing, rolling and patting work the small muscles of the hand, the same muscles a child uses to hold a spoon or a crayon. Let the child tear the bread into the bowl. Add one spoon of water yourself, then squeeze, roll and pat each piece into a little loaf, saying each action aloud. Then play the story together: “These loaves are hot, hot! Hands back!” Pull your hands back, blow “whoo, whoo”, and say “Warm now!” We never use raw flour or play dough, because raw flour can carry germs. A small flat taste, eaten sitting down, is fine. A whole ball in the mouth is not. To make it easier, make one big loaf with your hands over the child’s hands. To make it harder, make a big loaf and a little loaf. Five to ten minutes is plenty. Wash hands before and after.
activity.inClass: One adult sits at a table with up to four children. Ask about allergies first. Each child gets one slice of bread on a plate. The adult says one action at a time and everyone does it together: tear, squeeze, roll, pat. Then everyone plays “Hot, hot! Hands back!” together. Everyone washes hands before and after.
